page: Amazon Web Services c5d.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8275CL processor operating at 3.4 GHz, offering 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Compute resources are paired with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio. Unlike standard compute instances, the c5d family includes bundled local storage, providing 200 GB of NVMe SSD instance storage. Baseline network bandwidth is configured at 2 Gbps, and no GPUs are attached.

Benchmark results place the c5d.2xlarge solidly in the mid-range for general multi-threaded execution and data manipulation tasks. The system recorded a multi-core Geekbench score of 4511.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 8429.69, aligning with typical compute capabilities for an 8-vCPU instance. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 51.06 GB/sec, while write operations measured 39.32 GB/sec. However, single-core stress-ng throughput ranked in the bottom 25% with 1407.48, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression yielded 28.82 GB/sec, also falling in the lower quartile.

The presence of high-speed local NVMe storage and dedicated CPU cores delivers favorable resource density for latency-sensitive applications requiring temporary high-speed scratch space. In-memory workloads perform consistently, demonstrated by Redis SET operations processing 7.21 million operations per second and static web serving throughput hitting 6.66 GB/sec. Conversely, the machine demonstrates distinct performance tradeoffs in artificial intelligence workloads: LLM prompt processing on a medium 7B model scored 11.31 tokens/sec, placing it in the bottom 10%.

Given its hardware specifications and benchmark performance, the c5d.2xlarge is suited for software build environments, batch processing pipelines, static web serving, and distributed cache tiers. The included 200 GB NVMe drive makes it appropriate for logging nodes, temporary database staging, and CI/CD compile jobs that benefit from fast local disk access rather than remote block storage.

It integrates 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory and includes 200 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate steady middle-tier multi-core compute and memory bandwidth, posting a Geekbench multi-core score of 4511.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 8429.69. In-memory throughput is stable, evidenced by 7.21 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.66 GB/sec static web serving.
